BiblicalUsage: Esarhaddon was king of Assyria after his father Sennacherib, who was killed by his own sons in the temple of his god. His name means Ashur has given a brother, and the Bible names him twice: once in the story of Sennacherib's death, and once when the enemies of Judah claim he settled foreign peoples in Samaria. He rules an empire, but in Scripture he is only a marker on the edge of God's story with His people.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the kings of the earth are footnotes in God's story, not the other way round. Esarhaddon ruled an empire, yet the Bible remembers him only because of what God did with Judah.
RelatedPeople: Sennacherib, King of Assyria; King Hezekiah
